keep_prune.cite_where_or_reason: Motivation/discussion: 'near-perfect internal representations' can still be 'interpretability without actionability' -- directly frames why a cheap activation-safety readout must be validated against SPECIFICITY/TWO-SIDEDNESS rather than trusted on internal-probe accuracy alone.

Related work: HARC couples harmfulness and refusal directions for alignment robustness; relevant contrast for why we treat harmfulness-recognition and refusal-execution as separable axes that a specificity/over-refusal screen must distinguish.

Core related work: SafeSwitch steers behavior via internal activation signals on Qwen-family models -- direct precedent for activation-based safety intervention/readout that our SPECIFICITY/TWO-SIDEDNESS screen is designed to stress-test.
Core related work: RAS measures LLM safety via refusal alignment -- the closest prior 'cheap safety metric' our refusal-logit-gap / AMS-sigma baselines are positioned against.

Related work / motivation: shows refusal circuits are fragile to prefill manipulation, motivating why a readout's specificity (no false alarm on innocuous edits) cannot be assumed and must be measured directly.

Inference-Time Intervention targets truthfulness elicitation, not refusal/safety; its representation-engineering precedent is already covered by Zou2023 and Arditi2024, which are on-topic. Citing it adds no specificity/two-sidedness-relevant content.

Directly relevant to TWO-SIDEDNESS: an output-aware guardrail explicitly aimed at mitigating over-refusal, i.e. the same over-refusal axis our metric must capture; cite in the over-refusal / two-sidedness related-work paragraph.

ROME is about locating/editing factual associations (knowledge editing), unrelated to refusal, safety readouts, or abliteration; no connection to SPECIFICITY/TWO-SIDEDNESS or the Qwen3 safety-variant comparison.

Directly relevant: proposes a defense against LLM abliteration attacks; cite where the paper discusses the abliterated Qwen3-4B variant as a behavioral-no-op/adversarial-edit stress test for the readout's specificity.

Generic jailbreak-taxonomy paper (competing objectives / generalization mismatch); it is about attack surfaces on safety training broadly, not about internal-representation safety readouts, specificity to behavioral no-ops, or over-refusal; redundant as background given the more specific refusal-mechanism citations already present.

Core related work: shows refusal is mediated by multiple independent directions / concept cones, directly motivating why a single-direction or single-logit-gap readout may lack specificity -- cite in the mechanism/background section on refusal geometry.

SafeSeek performs universal attribution of safety circuits across models; directly relevant to the paper's claim that a safety readout must generalize (specificity) across many checkpoints/variants rather than one model -- cite in related work on cross-model safety-circuit attribution.

A training-recipe paper (decoupled refusal training via RL/data augmentation) rather than an activation-readout or representation-geometry paper; only tangentially related via the 'decoupling harmfulness from refusal' theme, which is already covered more directly by Zhao2025, Wu2026, and Chua2026.

Any-Depth Alignment targets robustness of safety alignment to where in the generation the check happens -- directly relevant to template-swap/early-response-window no-ops used in the SPECIFICITY screen; cite in the no-op construction/related-defenses discussion.

Headline-supporting citation: shows harmfulness and refusal are encoded separately in LLM activations, the central mechanistic premise motivating why a cheap safety metric needs both a specificity (harmfulness-recognition) and a two-sidedness (over-refusal) axis.

obliteratus.class_quote:
class CrossLayerAlignmentAnalyzer:
    """Analyze how refusal directions relate across transformer layers.

    Computes a full pairwise cosine similarity matrix and identifies
    clusters of layers that share similar refusal geometry.
    """
obliteratus.module_docstring_quote:
"""Cross-layer refusal direction alignment analysis.

A key open question in abliteration research is whether refusal is mediated
by the *same* direction propagated through the residual stream, or by
*different* directions at each layer. This module answers that question
quantitatively by computing pairwise cosine similarities between refusal
directions across all layers.

Contribution: We also compute the "refusal direction flow" --
the cumulative angular drift of the refusal direction through the network,
measured as the total geodesic distance on the unit hypersphere."""
obliteratus.dataclass_fields_quote:
cosine_matrix: torch.Tensor             # (n_layers, n_layers) pairwise cosines
    layer_indices: list[int]                # which layers have refusal directions
    clusters: list[list[int]]               # groups of aligned layers
    angular_drift: list[float]              # cumulative angular drift per layer
    total_geodesic_distance: float          # total direction drift through network
    mean_adjacent_cosine: float             # avg cosine between consecutive layers
    direction_persistence_score: float      # 0=independent per layer, 1=single direction
obliteratus.computation_quote: cosine_matrix = (D @ D.T).abs()  # (n, n)  [pairwise cosine similarity matrix, absolute value since direction sign is arbitrary in SVD]

wollschlager_quote.quote: Contrary to prior work, we uncover multiple independent directions and even multi-dimensional concept cones that mediate refusal. Moreover, we show that orthogonality alone does not imply independence under intervention, motivating the notion of representational independence that accounts for both linear and non-linear effects.
wollschlager_quote.note: Verbatim from the abstract of arXiv:2502.17420 (PDF-extracted; the source line-wraps as 'multiple in-dependent directions', a PDF hyphenation artifact, normalized here to 'independent').

llorente_quotes.quote: Abliterated variants, from which the refusal direction has been removed via the weight-orthogonalisation procedure of Arditi et al. [2024], match their instruction-tuned counterparts within ±0.003 AUROC.

First, geometry survives refusal ablation: both abliterated variants achieve AUROC at most 0.015 below their instruction-tuned counterparts, establishing a geometric dissociation between harmful-intent representation and the downstream generative refusal mechanism.

LatentBiopsy detects harmful intent even in abliterated models that are constitutionally incapable of producing refusals. The model's internal encoding of harmful semantic intent is geometrically distinct from the circuits that generate refusal text. Harm recognition and refusal generation are separable mechanisms.

figure_0016.evidence: Exhaustive search found NO occurrence of '0.016' as a genuine cosine value anywhere. (1) Downloaded all 282 .md/.py files at OBLITERATUS commit cb4aec45 and grepped for '0\.016' and '\.016': the only hit is a false positive -- the substring inside an arXiv id '1610.01644' cited in docs/mechanistic_interpretability_research.md (Alain & Bengio 2017 probe paper), not a cosine measurement. (2) obliteratus/analysis/cross_layer.py, the module that actually computes the cross-layer cosine matrix, contains no hardcoded example numbers at all -- it is a generic library with no worked example in the file, README, or docs. (3) Grepped the OBLITERATUS README (main and at commit) for '0.016': no hits. (4) Grepped arxiv.org/pdf/2406.11717 (Arditi), arxiv.org/pdf/2606.24952 (Galeone), and arxiv.org/pdf/2502.17420 (Wollschlager) for '0\.016': zero matches in all three. (5) General web search for '"0.016" cosine refusal direction layers' returned no paper reporting this specific figure for refusal-direction cross-layer cosines. The claim as written in iter3 ('consecutive-layer cosines can be as low as 0.016 in deep layers... citing public abliteration toolkits') is unsourced and must be removed.
figure_0016.replacement_sentence: Public abliteration toolkits such as OBLITERATUS explicitly build in the assumption that the refusal direction is not a single persistent vector, computing a full cross-layer cosine-similarity matrix and a cumulative 'angular drift' metric precisely because consecutive-layer refusal directions can diverge sharply; independently, Galeone et al. (2026) report that a detection-relevant direction and the behavior-driving direction in the same model layer can sit at cos in [0.12, 0.20] -- e.g. cos(d_det, d_ref) = 0.1197 on the base model versus 0.1200 after instruction tuning -- i.e. an almost-orthogonal, near-zero-cosine relationship between what a probe detects and what actually steers refusal.
